source.quote: Musical Fidelity's own page for the M6x DAC, read 2026-11-25. « 1x USB Audio Class 2.0, 'USB B'; up to 32 bit 768kHz (stereo PCM + MQA), DSD 256 (stereo DoP), DSD512 (stereo native) »; « 1x Coax, up to 24bit 192kHz (stereo PCM + MQA) »; « 2x Optical, up to 24bit 192kHz (stereo PCM + MQA) »; « 1x AES/EBU, up to 24bit 192kHz (stereo PCM + MQA) ». Bullet list: « USB: up to 32bit/768kHz »; « USB: DSD 256 (stereo DoP), DSD512 (stereo native) »; « SPDIF: up to 24bit/192kHHz » - the doubled H is the page's. « DAC Chip: 2x ES9038Q2M (dual differential) »; « Switchable Upsampling with Oversampling Bypass »; « Choose between 7 different digital filters and a complete oversampling bypass, disabling those filters. »

facts.chip: « 2x ES9038Q2M (dual differential) » - the same part as the M8x, which that page calls « dual mono ».

device_settings.why: « a complete oversampling bypass, disabling those filters » - the maker's own words, and « disabling those filters » is what makes `correctable` true rather than merely plausible.

_SEPT_filtres_ici_et_HUIT_sur_le_M8x_sur: « Choose between 7 different digital filters » against the M8x's « eight selectable digital filters », on two ES9038Q2M pairs from the same maker. Either the firmware exposes a different number, or one of the two pages is wrong. Nothing is resolved: both are quoted on their own records and neither count is carried across. The Pro-Ject Pre Box S2 Digital contradicted ITSELF on this in the same way, 7 against 8, three days ago.
